author: @oslubrinquez
text:
After watching Episode 7 (“The Bridge”), here’s my predicted death ranking for the finale — and hear me out, this lines up with what we just saw:

1. Kali – Her whole arc this season has been emotionally heavy and tied to Eleven’s choices. She’s basically pitching a suicide‑style plan with El to collapse the bridge forever, so her story feels like it’s heading for a tragic end. 

2. Eleven – She’s the core, but Episode 7 ends with her maybe agreeing with Kali’s plan. That hesitation feels like setup for huge risk — she might stay behind. 

3. Will – He’s emotionally connected and the group’s moral center now that he’s accepted himself publicly, but Vecna’s been targeting him personally before, and his connection to the bridge makes him a real target.

4. Steve – Out front in the group’s plan, right in the danger zone. His death would hit hard emotionally, especially because of his bond with Dustin—he’s been mentoring and protecting him all season, and Dustin would feel that loss deeply.

5. Hopper – Protective figure to Eleven and emotional anchor for the group; his survival is uncertain, especially if the story puts him in a sacrificial role to save Eleven.

6. Holly – Pulled around the Upside Down, nearly captured multiple times, and trapped in Vecna’s lair, her situation is extremely precarious. One wrong move and she could be gone in an instant.

7. Dustin – Usually clever and resourceful, but Episode 7 puts him in constant danger. With monsters on the move and Steve possibly sacrificing himself, Dustin could face life-or-death situations that test his limits.


Let’s see who actually makes it! Like this comment after the finale if my predictions are right—or roast me if they’re wrong.

P.S. I think most of the characters in top 5 wouldn't make it.

author: @Newone8-q9y
text:
Why Steve Harrington? Here's Why:

​The Likelihood: Extremely High
How he will die: Sacrificial Heroism.
Volume 1 has already leaned heavily into Steve’s growth as the "protector" of the kids. With the Duffer Brothers recently teasing his vulnerability (the "falling Funko Pop" incident), it feels like Steve’s arc—from selfish jock to selfless "babysitter"—is destined for a final sacrifice.
​The Theory: He will likely die in Volume 2 (Chapter 6 or 7) while holding back a swarm of creatures (perhaps the Mayan-inspired Camazotz mentioned in episode titles) to allow Dustin and the others to escape. It would be the ultimate "hero" moment that cements his legacy. Plus:

Steve Harrington: The "If You Die, I Die" Promise
​The Volume 2 trailer features a devastatingly foreshadowed line that has fans convinced Steve is done.
​The Dialogue: In a quiet, high-stakes moment, Steve looks at Dustin and says, "If you die, I die." In Stranger Things writing, these kinds of "blood brother" promises almost always precede a situation where one has to save the other at the cost of their life.
​The Setting: The trailer shows Steve, Dustin, Nancy, and Jonathan navigating the Upside Down version of Hawkins Lab. They are shown staring at a massive, glowing sphere of energy (likely the "bridge" to Dimension X).

​The "Camazotz" Connection: Episode 6 is titled Escape from Camazotz. If Steve is the one holding the line so Dustin can escape this mental/physical prison, the "If you die, I die" line becomes his final mission statement.
​The Duffer Brothers' Meta-Clue: During a recent appearance on The Tonight Show, the creators placed a Steve Funko Pop on the very edge of the desk. It fell off mid-interview. While it could be a troll, they have admitted Steve was originally supposed to die in Season 1—completing his "redemption" arc now would be their way of finally closing that loop.

text: I think the Mind Flayer represents the collective sadness and negative memories. One big theme this season feels like “the only way out is through.” Max can only return to Hawkins by going through her most painful memories. When she panics because she’s unable to escape, Henry appears, then when she runs to the cave, he can’t go through and seems terrified, because that’s where his worst memories live. It’s a really beautiful representation of how being stuck in a dark emotional place can feel, and how confronting it is sometimes the only way forward.

text: In a captivating cinematic moment that lasts approximately one minute and twenty seconds, viewers are thrust into an unsettling scene featuring the character Vecna. This scene weaves together elements from his earlier appearances in the series, specifically drawing upon his mystical and enigmatic presence exhibited through the peculiar Mr. Whats-It, as well as his haunting manifestation during the earlier narrative set within Hawkins Lab in 1979. As the sequence unfolds, a visually striking moment occurs where Vecna’s hand begins to undergo a grotesque transformation, morphing into the monstrous form that he ultimately assumes. This metamorphosis not only serves as a poignant illustration of his character's evolution but also reinforces the themes of horror and otherworldliness that permeate the narrative. Through this visual representation, the scene encapsulates the essence of Vecna’s character, effectively juxtaposing his earlier terrifying allure with the grotesque power he embodies in his fully realized form. Such a transition evokes a sense of dread and anticipation, compelling the audience to engage deeply with the underlying lore of the story's universe.

I find it hard to remember things after these time gaps. I would have preferred to „binge“ watch each season without too much time beween volumes‘ releases. Because I can’t wait to watch S5E1 until the end of the year without getting spoiled by Social Media or social environment. It’s so nasty. I feel like being forced to watch each new episode right after release to not get spoiled. But then, because of the large time gap between the volumes‘ releases it‘s hard to remember the content of the episodes that I watched a month ago. I find this release schedule by Netflix to be consumer-unfriendly. I miss the times when seasons were released as a whole so I could binge watch them.

"Everything we've ever assumed about the Upside Down has been dead wrong." 

The Upside Down isn't the real bad place but a bridge between the real world and the origin world of the mindfayer, demogorgons, etc. 

The reason El couldn't find Vecna and Holly & the demogorgon in the Upside Down is because they weren't in the Upside Down. 

The place Henry/1 got sent to may have been the origin world and when El opened a gate the second time she opened it to a bridge (the Upside Down) and that maybe explains why the bridge is stuck in the static real world replication of the day it got opened/day will went missing. 

The new world Vecna is envisioning might be a merging of 2 worlds, origin world and real world with the Upside Down serving as a bridge. The wormhole foreshadowing also kinda supports this theory.

text: At 0:14 max is climbing through the rocket ship playground into hollys room. You can see the bars beyond her feet. I would also like to point out that the first three scenes we see of holly and max (max climbing through the hole in hollys wall, max and holly looking down a large wooden shaft and max and holly stepping through a floating door) all directly parallel either 'Alice in wonderland' or 'Alice through the looking glass.' When max is climbing through the hole in hollys bedroom wall she is actualy climbing through the mirror on the wall (you can see shards of glass on the desk below. In  'Alice through the looking glass' Alice climbs through a mirror into a bizzare world that parallels her own, Alice leaves this world by falling asleep at the end of the book. It is importent to note that max is already in a sort of parallel world so perhaps she is climbing into the real one. This might be a stretch but the world alice ventures into when she climbs through the mirror is much more childish then the one she belongs in, but there is a hidden level of darkness to it, similer to the world max and holly are stuck in, also rocketship playgrounds are childish and max is climbing out of one. When max and holly look down the shaft it is similer to alice in wonderland because alice falls down a deep hole to get to wonderland. The door parallels alice in wonderland because throughout the book alice has to go through doors to reach different parts of wonderland.

author: @XOXO_123
text:
These are my very own strong theories about Season 5:

So, my first theory is that in season 1, during the dnd game between the boys in the last episode, we see that the Thessalhydra is brought into the game making Will fireball him and they eventually win. Mike mentions Lucas cutting off its 7 heads, Dustin placing them into his bag of holding and they carry the heads out of the dungeon, victorious! But, they ask about the Lost Knight and the Proud Princess which could refer to any of our main characters in the final battle (in season 5), moreover they talk about the weird flowers in the cave (we have seen plants and flowers being crafted for the upside down set in the broadcast channel back in September 2024 for season 5!). What if, all of these elements will be in the final battle? 
As we know, the Duffers have always been very detailed about connecting elements in a loop, so it makes sense to me that this just may work out.

My second theory is that Mama/Terry Ives will have some role in this season, either by helping out El and the team or by weakening Vecna with her powers through manipulation. There's NO way the Duffers would just leave her out with a flat context as seen in season 2.

Keep in mind, these are JUST MY OWN THEORIES, we could never predict the mysteriously intriguing work that the Duffers had in mind for this ONE LAST ADVENTURE. I absolutely love Stranger Things and will forever be grateful to the cast and crew for creating a masterpiece!
Lastly, to anyone reading this, please give me credit if you want to mention these somewhere else because I came up with these entirely by myself; I am really excited for Vol 2 and the Finale.

The trailer is so AWESOME. LIKE NO WORDS. WORDS CANNOT DESCRIBE THIS. But my thought is I really thought we were going to get mike's POV this volume, and that he would finally be an MC again(since he really hasn't been one since s2), since we haven't seen his POV since s2 ep9, not really, in terms of what's going on inside his head. Also, I am so so scared for Dustin and Steve, but I don't think they'll die since there's a leaked scene of Steve dropping off Dustin at college. I think there's going to be a fake-out death, maybe, for either one of them.
I hope we get a Suzie cameo at some point in the season cause she's so amazing.
Also, where are our 3 main main characters (I repeated main because they're the OG MC's) Will, El and Mike? I hope we get more scenes of them in vol.2 and the finale. 
I don't want anyone to die but it's INEVITABLE. 😭😭😭😭😭
Lastly, we saw Will's redemption arc, El's continued arc, and even Max, Steve, Hopper, Joyce, and everyone else's, but we still haven't seen Mike's arc since s2. Hope to see it in vol.2.
I get that this is a bit too long but I'm just rambling atp.

author: @Jdiroe
text:
Theory dump:

	1.	Steve and Dustin are safe. Narratively, their anchors removing either would collapse the emotional core of the group this late in the story.
	2.	The red/blue shockwave isn’t just visual flair. It resembles an anaglyph effect, implying two realities occupying the same space the Upside Down phasing into the Right Side Up rather than fully replacing it.
	3.	Robyn’s love interest appears to have a direct Demogorgon encounter, which may be intentional. The show often uses first-contact moments to establish stakes and catalyze character choices.
	4.	8 + 11 + 1 = 20. That number matters. In D&D terms, a natural 20 isn’t just success,it’s fate intervening. This could signal a turning point where probability breaks in the kids’ favor.
	5.	The portal Steve and Dustin witness doesn’t behave like previous gates. Its structure suggests either temporal displacement or access to Dimension X potentially the true origin space of the numbered children, possibly linked to Camazotz-like mythos.
	6.	Vecna is increasingly framed less as a final boss and more as a corrupted champion. The visual language and pacing suggest a Vader-style arc, not absolution, but a choice at the end that shifts the outcome.

This season feels less about defeating evil and more about reconciling fractured realities.
